name: Mother sauce system
summary: A system that derives all the sauces of a kitchen from a few base sauces. A cook who knows the base can make many small sauces from it.
how: Make each base sauce from a stock and a roux: espagnole, velouté and béchamel.
Add one item to a base sauce, such as herbs, wine or cream, to make a small sauce.
Keep the base sauces ready each day, and finish each small sauce to order.

origin.note: Carême set the grand sauces (espagnole, velouté, allemande and béchamel) as the base of his sauce chapters.

adoptions.via: Escoffier cut the grand sauces to five mother sauces in Le Guide culinaire.
